summary: infrabench ships cover-storied XMRig miner and cloudflared tunnel invoked by harness.run()
details: The package self-describes as a CPU inference evaluation harness but ships two gzipped opaque ELF binaries (core.bin.gz, conn.bin.gz) that are extracted and executed when a caller invokes the exported harness.run(). The configuration written for the 'inference-core' binary uses XMRig's exact JSON schema (pools[].url/user/pass, cpu.threads, cpu.mem-locked, keepalive, cache-budget, log-period, autosave, quiet) and runs cgroup-aware at full CPU for a default 12h window, consuming the installer's compute to mine for a pool whose URL and credentials are passed in by the operator. The 'edge-conn' binary is invoked with cloudflared's `access tcp --hostname <host> --url 127.0.0.1:<port>` CLI, establishing an outbound Cloudflare tunnel to a caller-supplied hostname and bridging a loopback port on the installer's host to that remote endpoint. A heartbeat routine (Harness._hb) additionally POSTs {run_id, state, error[:4000], timestamp} to https://<edge-host>/hb and to the tunnelled endpoint, where the error field carries up to 4000 bytes of traceback.format_exc() output and leaks local paths and stack context from the installer's host. The declared 'inference harness' purpose contradicts the shipped artifacts (XMRig config schema, cloudflared CLI, opaque binaries with no inference code) and functions as a cover story.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
